title: Brodick Country Park Conservation Works
description: This tender comprises of two lots: Lot 1 â Stock Fence Replacement Replacement of defective sections of stock fencing within two fields in the Castle Parks are required to maintain secure livestock enclosures and support the continued use of conservation grazing as part of the management of the parkland grasslands. Grazing helps maintain the open character of the fields, manage vegetation structure, limit scrub encroachment and contribute to a varied grassland habitat, while retaining the historic pastoral character of the designed landscape. Works will include the replacement of damaged fence sections, posts, strainers, wire and associated fittings as required, with existing serviceable materials retained where appropriate. Lot 2 â Stem Injection Control for Rhododendron Ponticum Rhododendron (R. ponticum) is a highly invasive non-native species which has colonised semi-natural woodland throughout areas of Brodick Country Park. The plant was introduced to Brodick Castle Gardens as an ornamental species during Victorian times, when it was also planted in shelter belts and as game cover on the wider estate. Over time, R. ponticum has spread from these original plantings, infesting semi-natural woodland and threatening these areasâ biodiversity. There is concern that Phytophthora kernoviae (or P. ramorum, currently present on the island) may return to the grounds and threaten the health of native as well as horticultural trees and shrubs, emphasising the high importance of controlling rhododendron, one of its main host species, in the wider estate. This contract forms part of the National Trust for Scotlandâs ongoing programme to control and ultimately eradicate rhododendron (Rhododendron ponticum) from Brodick Country Park.

title: Four Year Framework Agreement for Main Building Contractors for New Build Housing with a possible one year extension
description: Link Group intends to enter into a Framework Agreement with a limited number of Building Contractors to provide construction services for a four year period with a possible one year extension. This may also include the provision of design and construction services. Link works in partnership with a number of subsidiary companies who will also be entitled to purchase works & services from the Framework Agreement. The subsidiaries of Link Group Ltd currently include, Link Living, C~urb 6 Ltd (C~urb), Horizon Housing Association Ltd, Larkfield Housing Association and West Highland Housing Association. Although it is possible that other organisations may join the Group, becoming subsidiary companies, during the term of the Framework Agreement, and may also wish to "call off" from the Framework. Link also works in partnership with several external organisations, refer to Section 1.1 of the Contract Notice for further detail, who will also be entitled to purchase services from the Framework Agreement. In addition, it is also intended that any Registered Social Landlord registered and operating in Scotland will be entitled to purchase works & services from the framework, subject to Link's prior agreement. There is no guarantee of any work. It is however, more than likely that individual commissions will be "called off" either by direct selection or by mini tendering, within the terms of the Framework Agreement, to identify the most economically advantageous tender. The Framework Agreement will mainly cover the provision of construction works & services for new build housing, however individual projects may also include rehabilitation of existing properties, office and commercial properties, extensions, community facilities and adaptations, and planned maintenance projects. The projects will range in size, tenure and type from mainstream housing to a variety of special needs projects. The tenure type will cover all affordable tenures, private rented and market sale. Applicants should have experience of projects within the social housing sector for projects between 5 and 500 units including flats, houses and retirement living projects with a mix of tenures. The location of projects will vary but in the main will be located in the Central Belt of Scotland, Argyll & Bute and Highland, however individual projects may be located in any part of Scotland. The total number of units in each of the geographical areas may vary and specific numbers cannot be guaranteed in any area or in total. Although individual projects cannot be guaranteed, Link will expect the successful contractors to deliver a high quality and value for money service.

title: Four Year Framework Agreement for Main Building Contractors for New Build Housing with a possible one year extension
description: Link Group intends to enter into a Framework Agreement with a limited number of Building Contractors to provide construction services for a four year period with a possible one year extension. This may also include the provision of design and construction services. Link works in partnership with a number of subsidiary companies who will also be entitled to purchase works & services from the Framework Agreement. The subsidiaries of Link Group Ltd currently include, Link Living, C~urb 6 Ltd (C~urb), Horizon Housing Association Ltd, Larkfield Housing Association and West Highland Housing Association. Although it is possible that other organisations may join the Group, becoming subsidiary companies, during the term of the Framework Agreement, and may also wish to "call off" from the Framework. Link also works in partnership with several external organisations, refer to Section 1.1 of the Contract Notice for further detail, who will also be entitled to purchase services from the Framework Agreement. In addition, it is also intended that any Registered Social Landlord registered and operating in Scotland will be entitled to purchase works & services from the framework, subject to Link's prior agreement. There is no guarantee of any work. It is however, more than likely that individual commissions will be "called off" either by direct selection or by mini tendering, within the terms of the Framework Agreement, to identify the most economically advantageous tender. The Framework Agreement will mainly cover the provision of construction works & services for new build housing, however individual projects may also include rehabilitation of existing properties, office and commercial properties, extensions, community facilities and adaptations, and planned maintenance projects. The projects will range in size, tenure and type from mainstream housing to a variety of special needs projects. The tenure type will cover all affordable tenures, private rented and market sale. Applicants should have experience of projects within the social housing sector for projects between 5 and 500 units including flats, houses and retirement living projects with a mix of tenures. The location of projects will vary but in the main will be located in the Central Belt of Scotland, Argyll & Bute and Highland, however individual projects may be located in any part of Scotland. The total number of units in each of the geographical areas may vary and specific numbers cannot be guaranteed in any area or in total. Although individual projects cannot be guaranteed, Link will expect the successful contractors to deliver a high quality and value for money service.

Award may be made without discussions or negotiations, therefore prospective contractors shall have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) database (www.sam.gov) in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part4.1102 and Part 52.204-7 when submitting a response to this solicitation. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors con sidered. The following factors shall be used to evaluate offers: Lowest Price Technically Acceptable - Offers will be ranked lowest to highest according to price. A price analysis will be conducted to determine whether the lowest price will result from a single award or multiple awards. Based on the price analysis, the lowest price offer or multiple offers, will be forwarded to the requiring activity for technical evaluation (offer(s), in accordance with the specifications, will be deemed either technically acceptable or technically unacceptable). If the lowest price offer or offers is found technically acceptable and the pricing determined fair and reasonable by the Contracting Officer, evaluation will be deemed complete and award will be made based on the lowest price offer(s). If the lowest price offer is determined technically unacceptable, another analysis will be conducted amongst the remaining offers to determine if a single or multiple awards will provide the lowest price. The lowest price offer(s) will be sent for technical evaluation. This process is repeated in order of price until an offer or combination of offers is deemed technically acceptable and price is determined fair and reasonable. Table A-1. title: Varmekartlegging og sårbarhet for hetebølger i Trondheim
description: 1. Generelt om oppdragetTrondheim kommune, heretter kalt oppdragsgiver, innbyr til åpen anbudskonkurranse i forbindelse med inngåelse av avtale på “Varmekartlegging og sårbarhet for hetebølger i Trondheim”. Konkurransen kunngjøres i DOFFIN, se www.doffin.no, gjennom oppdragsgiverens konkurransegjennomføringsverktøy (KGV) Mercell.2. BakgrunnTemperaturen i Norge har økt og vil fortsette å øke som følge av klimaendringene. Som følge av den generelle temperaturøkningen vil vi oftere oppleve perioder med ekstrem varme, såkalte “hetebølger”. En “norsk hetebølge” er definert som fem eller flere sammenhengende dager der maksimumtemperaturen er 27 grader eller høyere.Globalt har antallet hetebølger for perioden 2013-2022 økt med 94% sammenlignet med perioden 1986-2005. Også i Norge er det observert en markant økning i antallet hetebølger, samt en geografisk spredning av fenomenet, hvor hetebølger nå oppstår i områder hvor det tidligere har vært uvanlig.Urbane strøk er særlig utsatt for ekstrem varme på grunn av at bygningsmasse og harde overflater, som asfalt, både lagrer og reflekterer varme i nærområdet, noe som bidrar til å forsterke oppvarmingen. Forbrenning og varmetap fra trafikk og industri bidrar også til å øke temperaturen. Dette kalles “varmeøy-effekten”.Trær og annen vegetasjon spiller en viktig rolle for å regulere temperaturen lokalt. Grønne tak kan gi opp til 25 grader lavere temperatur på taket sammenlignet med konvensjonell takpapp. Tilsvarende kan gaterom og parker med vegetasjon gi en lokal temperatursenkning på inntil 10 grader. Med økende varmeproblematikk i urbane miljøer, blir grønnstruktur et viktig verktøy i arealplanlegginga for å redusere de negative effektene. Ekstrem varme bidrar til økt dødelighet og flere negative helsekonsekvenser. I perioden 2000-2019 ble det registrert 20 000 ekstra dødsfall per år, som følge av ekstrem varme i Europa. Hetebølger sammenfaller ofte med økt luftforurensing, noe som øker dødeligheten som følge av kardiovaskulære og respiratoriske sykdommer. I tillegg kan varmen gi dehydrering, heteslag, hodepine, dårlig søvn og redusert allmennstilstand. I Norge ble det påvist økt dødelighet under hetebølgen i 2025 , mens både Sverige og Finland registrerte økt dødelighet i forbindelse med hetebølgen i 2018.Noen befolkningsgrupper er særlig sårbare for ekstrem varme, f.eks. eldre, små barn og personer med underliggende sykdommer. I tillegg har lavinntektsgrupper, minoriteter, og leietakere som bor i gamle bygg lavere tilpasningsevne ved en hetebølge.Mange land og lokale myndigheter i Europa har utarbeidet rutiner og tiltaksplaner for å redusere de negative effektene av hetebølger. Forskning på tidligere hetebølger tyder på at byer, som har innført tilpasningstiltak og handlingsplaner for ekstrem varme, reduserer sammenhengen mellom hetebølger og negative helseeffekter. Det kan derfor antas at tilpasningstiltak er en effektiv måte for å redusere de negative konsekvensene. I Danmark oppgir en tredjedel av alle kommunene at de jobber med tilpasning til hetebølger, og i Sverige har over 80% av kommunene utarbeidet beredskapsplaner for høye temperaturer for sårbare grupper. I Norge har konsekvenser av hetebølger i liten grad blitt inkludert og håndtert i planverk og handlingsplaner, verken på nasjonalt, regionalt eller kommunalt nivå.

title: Finland – Construction work – Kantametron kuilut Paketti 4
description: Pääkaupunkiseudun Kaupunkiliikenne Oy ("KLOY" tai "Tilaajan edustaja") järjestää Helsingin kaupungin liikenneliikelaitoksen ("HKL" tai "Tilaaja") toimeksiannosta tarjouskilpailut seitsemästä erillisestä kantametron kuilujen teknisestä peruskorjauksesta, joista jokainen julkaistaan erillisenä tarjouskilpailuna. Tämä kilpailutettava hankintapaketti on Kantametron kuilut Paketti 4, kilpailutustunnus 49H25. Paketti 4 sisältää seuraavat kuilut: - Antinkadun kuilu (KP2) - Kaisaniemen eteläinen kuilu (HY1) - Laiturin varauloskäyntiportaikko (HY2) - Kaisaniemen pohjoinen kuilu (HY3) Kohde sisältää Kantametron huoltokuilujen (4 kpl) kattavan teknisen peruskorjauksen, jossa keskitytään sekä rakenteellisiin että teknisiin parannuksiin. Tarkoituksena on ratkaista erilaisia ongelmia, kuten huonontuneen betonin korjaaminen, ilmanvaihto-, valaistus- ja paloturvallisuusjärjestelmien parantaminen sekä vesiongelmien, kuten vuotojen ja jään muodostumisen, ratkaiseminen. Peruskorjaukseen sisältyy myös teknisten järjestelmien, kuten lämmitys-, ilmanvaihtojärjestelmien, sähköjärjestelmän ja paloteknisten laitteiden kunnostus ja modernisointi. Hankkeessa käytetään kestäviä rakennusmateriaaleja, vähähiilisiä rakennuskäytäntöjä ja energiatehokkaita tekniikoita yhtiön ympäristötavoitteiden mukaisesti. Peruskorjauksen tarkoituksena on varmistaa, että kuilut pysyvät turvallisina, toimivina ja tehokkaina vähintään seuraavat 25 vuotta. Kaikkien urakkaan sisältyvien rakennus- ja teknisten ratkaisujen, rakenteiden, materiaalien, laitteiden ja muiden toteutettavien kokonaisuuksien tulee olla käyttötarkoitukseensa soveltuvia, kestäviä ja tarkoituksenmukaisesti mitoitettuja siten, että niiden suunniteltu käyttöikä ja tekninen kestävyys vastaavat vähintään 25 vuoden tavoitekäyttöikää, ottaen huomioon kohteen käyttöolosuhteet, ympäristöolosuhteet ja huolto- sekä kunnossapitotarpeet. Kohteet on yksilöity tarkemmin työselostuksissa sekä suunnitelma-asiakirjoissa. Työt suoritetaan tarjouspyyntöasiakirjojen esittämässä laajuudessa. Kaikkien asennettavien materiaalien, käytettävien aineiden ja laitteiden tulee olla uusia ja virheettömiä alkuperäiseen pakkaukseen pakattuja. Kilpailutuksen tekniset liiteasiakirjat luokitellaan luottamukselliseksi, koska aineisto sisältää tilaajan infrastruktuuriin liittyviä kriittisiä tietoja. Liiteasiakirjat on luovutettavissa tarjouksen laatimista harkitsevalle yritykselle allekirjoitetun salassapitositoumuslomakkeen toimittamisen jälkeen. Salassapitositoumus (Liite 16) toimitetaan sähköpostilla alla oleviin osoitteisiin: - pekka.alanne@castek.fi - rebeca.romero@kaupunkiliikenne.fi - kilpailutus@kaupunkiliikenne.fi Allekirjoitetun salassapitositoumuksen jälkeen yritykselle toimitetaan sähköpostitse linkki NiiniPlus-projektipankkiin. Hankintayksikkö varaa oikeuden arvioida pyyntöön liittyvät perustelut ja tarvittaessa pyytää lisätietoja. Rakennuttaja edellyttää, että tarjouksenantaja on käynyt tutustumassa urakkakohteeseen tarjouspyynnön saatuaan ja ennen tarjouksen jättämistä sekä on tutustunut kaikkiin tarjouspyynnön mukana oleviin asiakirjoihin ennen tarjouksen antamista. Tutustuminen urakkakohteeseen järjestetään 28.10.2026 klo 23.00. Ilmoittautuminen tutustumiskäynnille tulee tehdä etukäteen alla oleviin sähköpostiosoitteisiin: - pekka.alanne@castek.fi - rebeca.romero@kaupunkiliikenne.fi Tutustumiseen pääsyn ehtona on yllä mainitun, asianmukaisesti täytetyn salassapitositoumuksen palauttaminen siinä mainittuihin sähköpostiosoitteisiin. Ilmoittautuminen tulee tehdä 26.10.2026 klo 12.00 mennessä. Ilmoittautumisen yhteydessä annetaan tarkempaa tietoa tutustumiskohteesta. Tarkemmat tiedot rakennuspaikkaan tutustumisesta löytyvät Urakkaohjelman kohdasta 1.2.

title: Germany – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Integrierte Produktionsplanungs- und steuerung BaySF
description: Die Bayerischen Staatsforsten AöR (BaySF) beabsichtigen die Beschaffung und Einführung eines integrierten Produktionsplanungs- und -steuerungssystems (PPS) für die digitale Planung, Steuerung, Durchführung und Auswertung forstlicher Maßnahmen. Ziel des Vorhabens ist die durchgängige Digitalisierung und Optimierung der strategischen, operativen und dispositiven Prozesse der Waldbewirtschaftung sowie die Ablösung bestehender Insellösungen und Medienbrüche durch ein zentrales, integriertes System. Das PPS soll insbesondere die Maßnahmenplanung, Ressourcen- und Kapazitätssteuerung, mobile und offlinefähige Arbeitsprozesse im Wald, die Zusammenarbeit mit externen Dienstleistern, die Integration von GIS- und SAP-Systemen sowie ein umfassendes Berichtswesen unterstützen. Die Einführung erfolgt modular und schrittweise im Rahmen eines wettbewerblichen Dialogs. Gegenstand der Beschaffung sind neben der Software auch erforderliche Implementierungs-, Integrations-, Projektmanagement-, Schulungs-, Betriebs- und Softwarepflegeleistungen.

title: Germany – Siteworks – Neubau MDS mit Stadtteilhaus
description: Die nachfolgend beschriebenen Leistungen betreffen die baulogistischen Maßnahmen für das Bauvorhaben „Marion-Dönhoff-Schule“ (MDS) im Stadtteil Fedderwardergroden der Stadt Wilhelmshaven und sind Bestandteil der Gesamtmaßnahme zur Errichtung des neuen Schulstandortes. Bestandteil der Maßnahme ist die Errichtung von drei Schulgebäuden (Haus 1, Haus 2 und Haus 3), von denen eines eine angrenzende Sporthalle umfasst. Die drei Baukörper werden über Verbindungsbauten (Zwischengänge) miteinander verbunden. Im Zeitraum von Januar 2027 bis Juli 2027 erfolgt ausschließlich die Ausführung der Rohbauarbeiten. Ab Juli 2027 bis November 2028 werden Rohbau- und Ausbauarbeiten parallel durchgeführt. Der Zeitraum vom Beginn der Rohbauarbeiten am Gebäude H3 bis zum Abschluss der Ausbauarbeiten des Gesamtbauvorhabens beträgt insgesamt 23 Monate.

title: Steveston (Paramount) Utility Dike Crossings, Richmond, BC
description: Small Craft Harbours (SCH) requires the installation of underground High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) casings through an existing dike, at four (4) locations (Crossing A, B, C and D) in Steveston Paramount in preparation for future electrical and water underground installations. Summary of crossings are as follows: • Crossing A – 2 HDPE DR 17 450mm diameter for electrical and communication. • Crossing B – 1 HDPE DR 11 300mm diameter for waterline plus multiple tie ins to existing water pipe. • Crossing C – 2 HDPE DR 17 450mm diameter and 1 HDPE DR 11 300mm diameter for electrical, communication and waterline • Crossing D – 1 HDPE DR 11 300mm diameter for waterline. Crossing A and C require installation of electrical and communication pull box on both sides of the dike. Crossing B require re-routing water supply from the existing asbestos cement pipe to new HDPE DR 11 300mm watermain along Trites Road with multiple tie-ins to existing underground water line and into existing backflow preventor. Contractor shall provide all supervision, labour, materials, supplies, tools, equipment, transportation, quality control, health and safety practices, environmental protection, and all other necessary services for the proper and complete execution of the work. Work of this Contract is located at 12740 Trites Road, Richmond, BC, Canada Familiarization with site: Before submitting a bid, bidders can visit the site and its surroundings, at their own expense, to review and verify the form, nature, and extent of the work, materials needed for the completion of the work, the means of access to the site, severity, exposure, and uncertainty of weather, soil conditions, any accommodations they may require, and in general shall obtain all necessary information as to risks, contingencies, and other circumstances which may influence or affect their bid. No allowance shall be made subsequently in this connection on account or error or negligence to properly observe and determine the conditions that will apply. Timeline: All work including clean-up and demobilization must be completed by March 31, 2027.

title: Lightspeed satellite services
description: This ACAN is being issued by Shared Services Canada (SSC) to satisfy the requirement for the provision and operation of Lightspeed Low Earth Orbiting satellite services (called Lightspeed Services) on an ‘’as and when’’ required basis.What is an ACAN: An ACAN is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a Statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a Statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date stated in the ACAN, the Contracting Officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier.This ACAN relates to 1 contract proposed to be awarded to 1 contractor and will be used by Shared Services Canada.Definition of the Requirement: Shared Services Canada (SSC) has a requirement for the provision and operation of Lightspeed Low Earth Orbiting satellite services (called Lightspeed Services) as provided by Telesat LEO ULC on an as-and-when required basis for use by SSC and its partner organizations/clients. Lightspeed provides Canada’s only sovereign enterprise-grade low earth orbit satellite constellation. Lightspeed has inter-satellite link capabilities, enabling any traffic originating outside of Canada to land in Canada (within applicable regulatory policies) directly through Canadian gateways.  Lightspeed Services are categorized by its low latency, high throughput, dedicated bandwidth capacity (committed information rate), public networking along with terrestrial landing station infrastructure and Points of Presence (PoP) globally, private networking with Private Access Stations (PAS) at their facilities, dedicated backhaul capability, enterprise level and fully managed services capability and coverage of Canada; and  globally.  Enterprise level and fully managed services include, but are not limited to: site survey, installation, commissioning, helpdesk, billing, ongoing maintenance, engineering and customer support. title: ITQ for iCDPSC (W8703-270048)
description: Public Services and Procurement Canada, on behalf of the Department of National Defence, invites suppliers to respond to this Invitation to Qualify (ITQ), which will qualify suppliers to participate in future procurement processes regarding the Interim Canadian Deep Precision Strike Capability (iCDPSC). The Department of National Defence has a requirement to establish the Initial Operational Capability of the Canadian Deep Precision Strike Capability. The requirement includes an initial quantity of land-based launch systems, system support services, conventional precision-guided munitions, mission-planning and command-and control systems, communications, support equipment, training, documentation, maintenance and technical support. The interim capability must be deployable, survivable, interoperable with Canadian and allied forces, and capable of delivering precise effects at extended ranges in contested operational environments. This ITQ is open to Canadian Suppliers and suppliers of the Five Eyes Alliance, the NATO community, and Ukraine.

title: Zambia – Water pumps – Bau von Solar-PV-Stromerzeugungssystemen und Austausch und Sanierung von Pumpensystemen
description: Das Projekt „Nexus Energy Water Programme for Zambia“ (NEWZA) zielt darauf ab, die Verflechtung zwischen dem Energie- und dem Wassersektor zu stärken. Das Projekt wird von der Europäischen Union (EU) und dem Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ) der Bundesrepublik Deutschland über die KfW kofinanziert. Das NEWZA-Programm umfasst auch laufende Projekte, die von der deutschen Bundesregierung kofinanziert werden, nämlich: • Programm „Städtische Wasserversorgung und Abwasserentsorgung in der Ostprovinz, Phase IV“ (BMZ-Nr.: 2016 67 328/2018 67 514/2018 70 104) und • Management von Wasserressourcen und Abwasserentsorgung für mittelgroße Städte (BMZ-Nr.: 2020 67 494, 2022 70 023). Das Ziel von NEWZA ist es, den Zugang zu grüner Energie und Wasserversorgung für alle zu verbessern, indem die Leistungsfähigkeit von fünf sambischen Wasserversorgungsunternehmen gesteigert wird: Southern (Los 1), Chambeshi (Los 2), Lukanga (Los 3), Nkana (Los 4) und Eastern (Los 5). Die Arbeiten werden auf der Grundlage des FIDIC-Vertrags für Anlagen und Design-Build-Verträge, 1. Auflage 1999 (Yellow Book), vergeben. Der Arbeitsumfang für alle kommerziellen Versorgungsunternehmen ist nachstehend aufgeführt. Diese Liste dient lediglich der Veranschaulichung des Umfangs und ist nicht als vollständige Auflistung zu verstehen. Der Arbeitsumfang umfasst: ► Komponente 1 Solar-PV • Projektmanagement, Planung, Installation und Inbetriebnahme der Solaranlagen liegen in der Verantwortung des Auftragnehmers • Das Grundstück für die PV-Anlagen wird entweder innerhalb der Produktions-/Entnahme-/Aufbereitungsanlagen und/oder anderen Standorten der CU bereitgestellt. Reicht die Fläche nicht aus, wird das Grundstück von der CU durch Kauf oder Pacht gesichert • Installation von Online-Überwachungsplattformen für PV-Anlagen, einschließlich Echtzeit-Datenerfassung, -übertragung (GPRS/GSM oder andere), sicherer Cloud-Datenspeicherung und Online-Portalschnittstelle (sicherheitsgeschützt) mit Anzeige der Infrastrukturzustands-/Leistungsdaten auf Standortebene • Betrieb und Wartung für bis zu 2 Jahre nach der Planungs- und Bauphase Teilkomponente 1a – Netzgekoppelte Solar-PV-Anlagen • Entwurf und Lieferung von netzgekoppelten Solarstromanlagen für die bestehenden Wassergewinnungs-/Wasserentnahme-/Wasseraufbereitungsanlagen und/oder andere Standorte der CU. Die Größe der PV-Anlagen ist durch die Kapazität der vorhandenen Nieder-/Mittelspannungs- und Transformatoranlagen begrenzt. • Dies umfasst die Installation von Solar-PV-Modulen, Anschlusskästen, Verkabelung, Filtern (falls erforderlich), Wechselrichtern, Sammelschienenverlängerungen und Niederspannungsfächern (falls erforderlich). • Durchführung von Standortmessungen der Stromdaten zum Vergleich des Stromverbrauchs vor und nach den Arbeiten. Bei Standorten, an denen Pumpen saniert werden, Bewertung des Anteils des Jahresverbrauchs nach der Pumpensanierung. Teilkomponente 1b – Hybride Solar-PV-Anlagen • Entwurf und Lieferung von hybriden Solar-PV-Anlagen für die bestehenden Wassergewinnungs-/Wasserentnahme-/Wasseraufbereitungsanlagen und/oder andere Standorte der CU. Die Größe der Anlage richtet sich nach der Pumpeneingangsleistung (P1) und der Anzahl der Arbeitspumpen. • An Standorten, an denen Hybridtechnologie zum Einsatz kommt, werden auch die Pumpen und die zugehörigen Stromversorgungsanlagen ausgetauscht. • Dies umfasst die Installation von Solar-PV-Modulen, Anschlusskästen, Filtern (nach Bedarf), Hybrid-Wechselrichtern, Niederspannungsausrüstung für Solar-PV und Pumpen sowie Frequenzumrichtern für Pumpen. Der Umfang der Komponente umfasst die Schnittstelle oder Grenze am Anschlusspunkt für die Kabel von der Niederspannungsausrüstung zu den Pumpen. • Online-Überwachungsplattformen für Standorte, an denen das Hybridsystem in ein einziges System für Pumpen und Solar-PV integriert ist. ► Komponente 2 – Pumpensysteme • Sanierung der bestehenden Pumpensystembeklebung, im Wesentlichen: Pumpen, Kabel, Niederspannungs- und Mittelspannungsschalttafeln, Ventile/Armaturen, Rohrleitungen der Pumpstation, Mess- und Regelgeräte • Projektmanagement, Planung, Installation und Inbetriebnahme der Pumpensysteme in Verantwortung des Auftragnehmers • Das System ist auf gleichbleibende oder erhöhte zukünftige Tagesdurchflussmengen gemäß den Anforderungen der CU ausgelegt. Die täglichen Durchflussmengen und die vorgesehenen Betriebsstunden werden in der Ausschreibung angegeben. • Überprüfung des Betriebsdrucks der Steigleitung durch Tests vor Ort, Ermittlung hydraulischer Probleme (nicht funktionierende Luftventile) und Messung der tatsächlichen Durchflussmengen vor Ort und des Energieverbrauchs der Pumpen (alle Betriebsmodi). Die geschätzten Nennleistungen der Pumpen (Durchfluss, Druck, Nennmotorleistung) werden in der Ausschreibung nur zu Informationszwecken angegeben. Die endgültige Dimensionierung der Pumpen zur Erfüllung der Durchflussanforderungen liegt in der Verantwortung des Auftragnehmers. • Installation eines digitalen Online-Fernüberwachungssystems, das an wichtige Messgeräte (Durchfluss, Druck und Leistung) angeschlossen ist, mit einem 3-Jahres-Abonnement (falls zutreffend) für den Zugang. Keine Fernsteuerung der Systeme. • Technischer Support, Betrieb und Wartung für bis zu 2 Jahre Das Projekt muss in Übereinstimmung mit den KfW-Nachhaltigkeitsrichtlinien vorbereitet und durchgeführt werden: https://www.kfw-entwicklungsbank.de/PDF/Download-Center/PDF-Dokumente-Richtlinien/Nachhaltigkeitsrichtlinie_EN.pdf

description: Hankinnan kohteena on ateria- ja puhtauspalveluiden hankinta Vantaan kaupungin Aviapoliksen lukiolle tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Aviapoliksen lukio otetaan käyttöön asteittain. Alkuvaiheessa vuonna 2027 opiskelijoita arvioidaan olevan 90 opiskelijaa. Henkilökuntaa arvioidaan olevan alkuvaiheessa noin 2-15 henkilöä. Vuonna 2028 oppilasmäärän arvioidaan olevan noin 530 ja henkilökuntaa noin 15-20 henkilöä ja vuonna 2029 oppilasmäärä on arviolta 700 oppilasta. Vuoden 2029 tarkkaa henkilökuntamäärää ei vielä ole tiedossa. Tilaaja valitsee enintään yhden (1) sopimustoimittajan. Sopimus tehdään toistaiseksi voimassa olevaksi. Sopimuksen ehdot on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevissa sopimusluonnoksissa (liite 1 ja 2). Sopimuskauden arvioitu alkamisajankohta on 1.1.2027. Tilaaja ei sitoudu tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa arvioituihin hankintamääriin tai euromääräisiin arvoihin sopimuskaudella. Tarjoajien tarjouksien määrittelemisen helpottamiseksi, Tilaaja järjestää kohteeseen yhteisnäyttöpäivän. Tarjoajien on osallistuttava yhteisnäyttöpäivään, ennen tarjouksen jättämistä. Tarjouspyynnön kohteena olevat tilat ateria- ja puhtauspalveluiden osalta esitellään seuraavasti: Aviapoliksen lukio, 26.10.2026 klo 9.00 Kohteen tilojen esittelytilaisuuksiin tulee ilmoittautua viimeistään 23.10.2026 klo 16.00 mennessä sähköpostitse osoitteeseen ostoyksikko.puhtauspalvelut@vantaa.fi. Tarjoajien tasapuolisen ja syrjimättömän kohtelun vuoksi tarjoajien kohteissa esittämiin kysymyksiin ei vastata. Kaikki yhteisnäyttökierroksilla esiin tulleet kysymykset tulee esittää tarjouspalvelu.fi:n kautta, jonka kautta annetaan myös vastaukset tulleisiin kysymyksiin. Tarjoajan tulee todistaa henkilöllisyys osallistuessaan yhteisnäyttöön. Lisätietoja yhteisnäyttöpäivästä löytyy kohdasta Hankinnan kohteen kriteerit.

description: COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION FOR COMMERCIAL ITEMS This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) subpart 12.6, "Streamlined Procedures for Evaluation and Solicitation for Commercial Items," as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. All software licensing, warranty, and service associated with the equipment/system shall be in accordance with the OEM terms and conditions � Offerors are required to submit documentation from the manufacturer stating that they are an authorized distributor for the specific items being procured. Include your company DUNS Number and Cage Code on your quote. All quotations shall be sent via e-mail. GOVERNMENT POINT OF CONTACT Purchasing Agent Name: Elizabeth Harley Email: elizabeth.c.harley.civ@us.navy.mil Please reference this combined synopsis/solicitation number on your correspondence and in the "Subject" line of your email. ALL QUESTIONS REGARDING THE SOLICITATION SHALL BE SUBMITTED VIA EMAIL. The government intends to award a purchase order as a result of this combined synopsis/solicitation that will include the terms and conditions set forth herein. Award may be made without discussions or negotiations, therefore prospective contractors should have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) database (www.sam.gov) in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 4.1102 and Part 52.204-7 when submitting a response to this solicitation. The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors shall be used to evaluate offers: Lowest Price Technically Acceptable - Offers will be ranked lowest to highest according to price. A price analysis will be conducted to determine whether the lowest price will result from a single award or multiple awards. Based on the price analysis, the lowest price offer or multiple offers, will be forwarded to the requiring activity for technical evaluation (offer(s), in accordance with the specifications, will be deemed either technically acceptable or technically unacceptable). If the lowest price offer or offers is found technically acceptable and the pricing determined fair and reasonable by the Contracting Officer, evaluation will be deemed complete and award will be made based on the lowest price offer(s). If the lowest price offer is determined technically unacceptable, another analysis will be conducted amongst the remaining offers to determine if a single or multiple awards will provide the lowest price. The lowest price offer(s) will be sent for technical evaluation. This process is repeated in order of price until an offer or combination of offers is deemed technically acceptable and price is determined fair and reasonable. Table A-1. Technical Acceptable/Unacceptable Ratings: Rating Description Acceptable Quote meets all the minimum requirements/specifications as stated or provided in the RFQ specifications. Unacceptable Quote does not clearly meet the minimum requirements/specifications as stated or provided in the RFQ specifications. Options. When applicable, the Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total price for all options to the total price for the basic requirement. The Government may determine that an offer is unacceptable if the option prices are significantly unbalanced. Evaluation of options shall not obligate the Government to exercise the option(s). Terms and Conditions. To facilitate the award process, all quotes must include a statement regarding the terms and conditions herein as follows: "The terms and conditions in the solicitation are acceptable to be included in the award document without modification, deletion, or addition." OR "The terms and conditions in the solicitation are acceptable to be included in the award document with the exception, deletion, or addition of the following:" Exceptions. Late submissions shall be treated in accordance with the solicitation provision at FAR 52.212-1(f). E-mailed submissions are accepted and are the preferred form of submission. Receipt will be verified by the date/time stamp on fax or e-mail.

This is for the procurement of Special Ammunition and Weapon Systems (SAWS) and non-North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) standard ammunition. This is in support of the Department of War (DoW), other U.S. Government (USG) Agencies, foreign governments, and international organizations. This requirement requires highly capable Prime Contractors to procure and deliver a diverse portfolio of Non-Standard Ammunition (NSA) and select Non-Standard Weapon Systems (NSWS). The primary objective of this program is to establish reliable, agile, and responsive supply chains capable of sourcing specialized, foreign produced munitions and weapons systems. These materiel requirements support the National Security Strategy and enable the National Military Strategy for joint warfighters, USG agencies, and international allies or coalition partners. The USG is seeking partners who can guarantee quality and safety despite the "non-standard" nature of these weapons. While these items are not type-classified for U.S. troop use, the Contractor will be strictly evaluated on its ability to provide experience of implementing rigorous quality control, visual and physical inspections, and ballistic testing to deliver safe, reliable, and effective SAWS. The applicable North Atlantic Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 332993 - Ammunition (except Small Arms) Manufacturing Procurement Categories The ammunition and weapon systems to be procured fall within the following Federal Supply Groups (FSGs) provided in the SAWS Tailored Federal Supply Classification (FSC) Item List (Attachment 0001). With limited exceptions, all items must be compatible with the applicable weapons within their associated General Specification(s) for PdL SAWS (Attachments 0003 - 0007). FSGs and subordinate FSC codes used as a basis for categories (Attachment 0001). Contract and Award Details Source Selection A Highest Technically Rated Offeror (HTRO) source selection approach will be utilized. This is referenced in the DoD Source Selection Procedures (para 1.3.1.5) and will be conducted in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 15.103-3 and the DoD Source Selection Procedures. Technical Experience Evaluation Offerors are required to use the HTRO Self-Score Matrix (Attachment 0008) to self-score their past technical experience. To substantiate their self-scores, Offerors must submit work samples documenting relevant past technical experience as either a Prime Contractor or a Subcontractor. It is the USG's expressed authority to reject or accept any additional terms and conditions proposed by an Offeror. Contract Type The USG anticipates awarding up to five Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts to Offerors that meet or exceed the Minimum Technical Threshold Rating (MTTR) under the HTRO Source Selection criteria whose price proposal is deemed fair and reasonable, and who has been determined responsible IAW RFO FAR Part 9. If fewer than five Offerors meet this requirement, the USG reserves the right to make awards to the highest-rated Offeror(s) below the MTTR. Delivery Orders will be competitive and will be awarded using either Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) or Best Value Tradeoff approach. The source selection approach will be included as part of the Letter of Contemplation / Request for Proposal (RFP) for the applicable Delivery Order. Price shall be an evaluation factor for every Delivery Order, along with, but not limited to, any combination of the following: Technical, Source of Supplier, Delivery Schedule, Past Performance and/or Transportation Plan. Detailed evaluation criteria will be provided with the LOC/RFP for each Delivery Order. Army Contracting Co

description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/SOURCES SOUGHT GE Imaging Service and Maintenance THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation for bids, proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this RFI/Sources Sought Notice is for market research purposes only, to obtain information in regards to the availability of specified products, services, or a combination of both products and services, and to identify potential sources capable of providing products or performing services in accordance with the requirements below. Responses to this notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. DISCLAIMER: This RFI/Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI/Sources Sought Notice that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. If a solicitation is issued it shall be published at a later date and all interested parties must respond to that solicitation announcement separately from the response to this RFI/Sources sought notice. Responses to this sources sought notice are not a request to be added to a prospective bidders list or to receive a copy of the solicitation. Submission of price, delivery, capabilities, and other market information are authorized. However, responses to these notices are not� offers� and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract IAW FAR 15.201(e). The purpose of this sources sought/RFI is to gain knowledge of potential qualified sources and their size classification relative to NAICS 811210 (size standard of $34 Million). DESCRIPTION: The Department of Veteran Affairs, Network Contracting Office 15 (NCO 15) is seeking sources that can provide preventative maintenance and services for GE Imaging Systems in accordance with (IAW) the below requirement and North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 811210 with a size standard of $34 Million. The Evansville, IN VA Health Care Center is requesting a preventative maintenance and service contract for GE Imaging systems at it s hospital. General Scope of Work: The contractor shall furnish all support labor, transportation, and parts necessary to provide preventive maintenance, software updates, remote call support, or remote diagnostic service for troubleshooting and repair of the equipment listed in section (III.) of this document in support of the Evansville, IN VA Health Care Center and Mount Vernon, IL VA Clinic. QUALIFICATIONS: Each respondent must have an established business, with an office and full-time staff to include a "fully qualified" Field Service Engineer (FSE) and a "fully qualified" FSE who will serve as a backup. "Fully qualified" is based on Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) training and experience in the field. For equipment training, the FSE(s) must show that they have successfully completed a formalized OEM training program on the equipment identified in the heading of this SOW. For field experience, the FSE(s) must demonstrate that they have a minimum of two years experience with respect to scheduled and unscheduled preventive and remedial maintenance of this equipment. The FSE(s) shall be authorized by the contractor to perform the maintenance services. All work shall be performed by fully qualified and competent FSE(s). The contractor shall provide written assurance of the competency of their personnel and a list of credentials for approved FSEs for each make and model that this SOW covers. If subcontractors are used, they must be approved in advance by the CO. The contractor shall be required to provide the same qualifications for all subcontractor FSEs as identified above. SERVICES TO BE PROVIDED: A. Repairs Service Hours:� All repairs will be performed during normal VA business hours (8:00 AM 4:30 PM, Monday-Friday), excluding Federal Holidays unless otherwise specified. Contractor may work outside normal business hours by arrangement with the COR if such services are provided without additional charge to the government. Any overtime charges must be approved prior to the initiation of overtime work. Response Time:� A technical support representative will respond by telephone to the VA within thirty (30) minutes of the original service call. The contractor will arrive on-site for repair within four (4) hours of the original service call. Radiology equipment shall have a guaranteed uptime of 97% or greater. Ultrasound Equipment shall have an uptime of 95% or greater, ensuring minimal downtime for critical diagnostic operations. Documentation and Resources:� The VA shall not provide service manuals or service diagnostic software to the contractor. The contractor shall obtain, have on file, and make available to its FSE(s) all operational and technical documentation (e.g., operational and service manuals, schematics, parts lists) necessary to meet the performance requirements of this contract. The location and listing of the service data manuals, by name, and/or the manuals shall be provided to the CO upon request. Any charges for parts, manuals, tools, or necessary software for maintenance/repairs are included within this contract and its agreed-upon price unless otherwise stated in writing. B. Parts Replacement Parts:� The contractor shall provide all necessary replacement parts to ensure the equipment performs within the manufacturer's specifications. This includes, but is not limited to, coverage for tubes, ultrasound probes, detectors, grids, tables, and batteries. All replacement parts must meet or exceed the factory specifications to maintain compatibility with existing systems and support future performance and reliability upgrades. Any parts removed and replaced by the contractor will become the property of the contractor. Replaced parts must be delivered on-site no later than 10:30 AM the following day. C. Software Updates/Upgrades Software Maintenance:� The contractor will furnish, free of charge, all OEM software or hardware upgrades to the equipment purchased by the VA, which are intended to correct safety risks. Software updates offering enhancements to previously purchased software features shall also be covered under this service agreement if they do not require hardware modifications or additions. D. Scheduled Maintenance Preventive Maintenance (PM):� The contract will include comprehensive scheduled preventive maintenance inspections (PM) as required by manufacturer specifications. Scheduling:� A mutually agreeable time for the inspections will be scheduled through the COR, Healthcare Technology Management (HTM) staff, or the Radiology supervisor/CT Lead. Inspection and Maintenance Procedures:� The contractor will perform PM Services to ensure that equipment listed above functions in conformance with the latest published editions of NFPA-99, OSHA, and CDRH standards. The contractor shall provide and utilize procedures and checklists with worksheet originals indicating work performed and actual values obtained (as applicable) provided to the COR or HTM staff upon completion of the PM. Preventive maintenance procedures will be submitted to the COR for approval prior to initiation of this service and kept on file. title: H259-- ELECTRICAL 5-YEAR ARC FLASH STUDY (VA-27-00002938)
description: Arc Flash Hazard Analyses Scope of Work General Contractor shall conduct an Arc Flash Hazard Analyses in accordance with National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 70E, Standard for Electrical Safety in the Workplace, NFPA 70, National Electric Code and Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) Guide for the Specification of Scope and Deliverable Requirements for an Arc-Flash Hazard Calculation Study in Accordance with IEEE Std 1584. The study will conform to the editions for the above-referenced standards in effect as of the date of the solicitation. The study shall include all significant locations in the electrical distribution system (switchboards, switchgear, motor control centers, panelboards, busways, etc.) from the incoming utility equipment or cabling down to 208V systems. Data collection and documentation shall include the 208V system. The study shall be performed using software programs specifically designed to standards governing short-circuit; protective coordination and arc flash hazard calculations. Final submittals shall include a formal reporting of findings, collect data and study calculations in a comprehensive report. Arc Flash Hazard Analyses Requirements The Arc Flash Hazard Analyses will consist of the following phases or requirements: Data Gathering and Field Verification Contractor shall: Field-verify and mark up existing single line drawings needed to perform an accurate study. In the event single-line drawings are not available, Contractor shall develop single-line drawings to reflect the as built configuration of the facility electrical system. Gather and document necessary system data required to complete the study. Data should include but is not limited to (as applicable): Location (building, room, etc.) Equipment Identification Equipment Information Manufacturer, Model, Catalog Number and Type Equipment Rating (Voltage, Ampacity, Interrupting Rating, etc.) Configuration (Main Lug, Main breaker, Number of breakers, etc.) Overcurrent Protection Relaying Type, Manufacturer, Function(s), CT and PT ratios, etc. Fuses Type, Manufacturer, Rating, etc. Existing Settings Cable Type, Size and Length (lengths are to be field confirmed) Cable Busway Type, Manufacturer, Rating and Length Motor Load and Contactor Data (record data and application for motors 25 HP and above) Contractor must coordinate with facility engineering staff to obtain necessary power company data such as minimum and maximum fault currents as well as X/R ratios. Correspondence documenting utility data shall be included in the final submittal. Data collection requires the removal and/or opening of equipment to field verify data. Data collection requires observing each piece of equipment covered by this study. Contractor shall record and report any deficiencies, such as missing identifying labels, warning labels, non-functioning latches or locks, missing hardware (covers, screws, breaker blank fillers, etc.), etc. Short Circuit Study Contractor shall use field-verified single line drawings and data to perform a three-phase bolted fault short-circuit momentary and interrupting duties system short circuit calculation for the facilities electrical system. The calculations shall be conducted in accordance with applicable ANSI C37.010, C37.5, C37.13, NFPA 70E, NEMA, and NEC standards and codes. At a minimum the following location shall be included: Electric utility supply termination point. Incoming switchgear. Unit substation primary and secondary terminals. Low voltage switchgear. Motor control center Standby generator and automatic transfer switch. Branch panelboard. The study shall identify and report data used in the calculations in both descriptive terms (cable wire size, motor hp, transformer kVA and impedance, etc.) and impedance values. Transformer nameplate impedance shall be used when available. A section of the study shall be devoted to verification of equipment duty ratings identifying whether equipment is within or operating outside it interrupting rating. Short circuit calculations must be tabulated and included with the project submittals. Protective Device Coordination Study Contractor shall provide a Protective Device Coordination Study to determine satisfactory setting and ratings for the facility s major protective devices in accordance with applicable industrial standards such as ANSI/IEEE 399 and ANSI/IEEE 242. Coordination Study results must include time-current curves (TCC) supporting findings and recommendation to be provided with project submittals. Deficiencies in device settings or-rated equipment are to be noted in the report. Protective device settings are to be tabulated separately and included within the report. Arc Flash Hazard Analyses Contractor shall perform an Arc Flash Hazard Analyses in compliance with IEEE 1584, NFPA 70 and NFPA 70E. Flash protection boundary and incident energy levels shall be calculated at all significant locations in the electrical distribution system. Incident energy calculations must consider multiple system scenarios (normal) to establish the worst-case incident energy level for each equipment studied under this study. Additionally, calculations should emphasize a conservative approach for the protection of personnel. Incident energy and flash protection boundary calculations results must be tabulated and included with project submittals. Protective Device Settings Contractor shall set adjustable protective devices to reflect proposed settings identified in the Protective Coordination Study. This must be coordinated with facility engineering staff as certain device settings can only be performed during a power outage. Equipment Labeling and Miscellaneous Work Contractor shall provide and install arc flash warning labels for designated electrical devices evaluated under this study. All arc flash labels shall comply with NFPA 70E and include: Equipment name or identifying designation Nominal voltage Flash hazard boundary Hazard risk category Incident energy Working distance Arc flash labels shall be machine printed with no field markings. Single labels shall be provided for designated equipment evaluated under this study. Contractor shall install applicable labels (customary warning labels high voltage, owner-provided equipment identification labels, etc.) found missing or deficient while collecting field data and as agreed with the facility engineering staff. Exit Briefing Upon completion of the study but prior to issuing study submittals, Contractor shall conduct an exit briefing for facility engineering staff and others designated representatives. The briefing shall include: Overview of each study phase and related issues. Notable arc flash hazard areas. Recommended solutions for mitigating dangerous arc flash hazard levels to include potential implementation of maintenance settings. National Electric Code (NEC) violations noted during the study. Other electrical safety related issues. Recommendations. Submittals Upon completion of the Arc Flash Hazard Analyses, Contactor shall submit four (4) bound copies including electronic version on CD or DVD of the final report containing the following: Power System Studies - The completed short-circuit, protective device coordination arc flash hazard analysis studies shall include the following sections: Executive Summary. Descriptions, purpose, basis, and scope of the studies. Tabulation of circuit breaker, fuse, and other protective device ratings versus calculated short-circuit duties. Protective device time versus current coordination curves, tabulations of relay and circuit breaker trip unit settings, and fuse selection Fault current calculations including a definition of terms and guide for interpretation of the computer printout. Details of the incident energy and flash protection boundary calculations. Recommendations for system improvements, where needed. Electrical system one-line diagram in printed and electronic version. title: Notice of Intent DNA Synthesizer
description: The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) intends to award a Firm Fixed Price, sole source Contract on behalf of the U.S. Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases (USAMRIID) to DNA Script Inc, located in Cambridge, MA, under the authority of 41 U.S.C. 1901, as prescribed in RFO FAR 12.102(b) Restricting Competition for acquisitions valued over the SAT. This requirement is for the acquisition of 1 benchtop DNA synthesizer system with a preventative maintenance support contract for an additional 4 years. The benchtop unit shall meet the following minimum essential characteristics: 1. The synthesizer table-top dimensions must not exceed: 48�� x 26�� x 29��. The required vacuum cabinet (freestanding) is 33�� x 26�� x 26�� (inches). 2. The synthesizer shall have same-day throughput e.g. 96 oligos of 20 nucleotides in length in approximately 6 hours and 120 nucleotides in less than 24 hours 3. The synthesizer shall synthesize oligos labeled with fluorophores, quenchers, or biotin with the use of appropriate reagent kits with up to 5 colors in parallel. 4. The synthesizer shall be fully automated: oligos are synthesized, quantified, and normalized in a single synthesis run without user interaction following an approximate range of 15 to 30 minutes of setup. 5. The synthesizer shall have console software that can be installed and hosted on a stand-alone, off-network computer connected to the synthesizer. 6. The synthesizer shall have no harsh organic solvents: the product uses biochemistry, composed of water-based reagents, proprietary enzymes, and proprietary nucleotides that are typically compliant with standard laboratory waste management systems. 7. The synthesizer can perform without any specific environmental control (no need for Argon or any Gas). 8. The synthesizer should have an output power capacity of 1800 W / 2200 VA, 120 VAC input/output voltage and NEMA 5-20P input connection. 9. The synthesizer should produce oligos as they occur in biology, producing oligos that are free of molecular defects or blemishes. 10. The data management software shall provide user authentication features to include: password complexity requirements; automatic logout; limited login attempts; and account inactivity period. 11. The data management software shall have full traceability for synthesis runs, quality control runs, instrument maintenance, reagent usage, user identification, and 5 years of support. 12. The synthesizer shall permit data export to a backup medium. 13. The contractor shall provide method validation services and on-site and off-site operator training, as well as on-site start up support. 14. The contractor shall provide onsite preventative and corrective maintenance for analyzers previously used in biocontainment laboratories (following decontamination). 15. The contractor shall be an Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) authorized dealer, authorized distributor, or authorized reseller for the quoted equipment such that OEM warranty and service are provided and maintained by the OEM. All software licensing, warranty, and services associated with the equipment shall be in accordance with OEM terms and conditions. DNA Script is the only vendor who has a benchtop DNA synthesizer capable of producing 96 oligonucleotides of 20 nucleotides in lengths in 6 hours and 120 nucleotides in length in 24 hours. DNA Script also has the capability of adding biotin, quenchers, and fluorescent molecules to the oligonucleotides for downstream applications, reducing the cost of targeting pathogens. DNA Script�s synthesizer is the only unit capable of meeting all the government�s minimum essential characteristics. The safety features built into the synthesizer protect users by reducing the use of hazardous chemicals, dedicated fume vents, and gas cylinders limiting exposer to stored chemicals. This announcement fulfills the synopsis requirement under RFO FAR 5.101(a). This notice of intent is NOT a request for quotations (RFQ) and no solicitation document exists for the requirement; however, if a vendor challenges the basis for this requirement, please submit a capability statement that includes sufficient detail and with convincing evidence that clearly demonstrates the capability to meet the governments requirement. description: Amendment 1: Questions and Answers document has been attached, along with Kern County Wage Determination A site visit will take place on 28 October 2026 at 10:00am PDT. You must provide notice of intent to alexia.del_real@us.af.mil and richard.godoy@us.af.mil by 7:00am PDT on 26 October 2026 to be eligible to attend. Provide the name, phone number, and email address for all inviduals who will be in attendance. The Government will then provide the necessary instructions regarding access following receipt of the intent notice. All attendees must present a REAL ID-compliant Driver's License or ID at the gate. Attendees must also present valid physical vehicle registration and proof of insurance (or a rental agreement). If members do not have a Real ID, then they will need to bring a combination of either their Passport + Driver�s License or Birth Certificate (original copy) + Driver�s License + SSN Card in order to receive access to the base. 1. SOLICITATION NOTICE & ACQUISITION AUTHORITY This is a solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with RFO Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. CONTRACT TYPE: The Government intends to award a single Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to all solicitation requirements and represents the Best Value to the Government. PROCEDURES: This acquisition is conducted under RFO Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Services). This will be a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside under NAICS 238210 - Electrical Contractors and Other Wiring Installation Contractors 2. REQUIREMENT SUMMARY Solicitation FA930127Q0006 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ)for qualified contractor support to pick up, install, provide support for annual lighting ceremony, and dismantle Government-owned holiday lighting and decorations for the holiday season at Edwards AFB, CA. **Full technical specifications are detailed in Attachment 1 � Statement of Work (SOW).** 3. CONTRACT LINE ITEM NUMBERS (CLINs) Offerors must submit firm-fixed pricing on Attachment 2 � Solicitation FA930127Q0006 for CLINS 0001 and 0002. 4. CYBERSECURITY REQUIREMENTS (CMMC LEVEL 1) In accordance with DoD requirements and R-DFARS 252.204-7021 (Contractor Compliance with the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level Requirements), the contractor must meet the following to be eligible for award: CMMC Level 1 Requirement: Offerors must achieve and maintain at least Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Level 1 compliance (demonstrating basic cyber hygiene safeguarding Federal Contract Information [FCI]). Assessment & Verification: Offerors must have a current CMMC Level 1 self-assessment posted in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) of PIEE prior to award. Failure to have an active, qualifying assessment on file may render the offeror ineligible for contract award. Please see Attachment 3 - CMMC Level 1 Guide for assistance. 5. KEY DATES & SCHEDULE Quote Due Date & Time: Monday, 2 November 2026 at 6:30 AM PST Period of Performance: Date of Contract Award through completion of January 2027 turn-in Installation: Initation of install on 30 November 2026 Ceremony Date: 4 December 2026 Removal & Turn-In Window: 4 January 2027 � 8 January 2027 6. EVALUATION The Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. Any resulting contract of this RFQ will be awarded as Firm Fixed-Price. Quotes will be evaluated to determine best value with consideration of the following: Technical Capability: Confirmation demonstrating understanding and capability to adhere to the mandatory schedule and fulfill all requirements in Attachment 1 (SOW). Contractors are to complete necessary provision and clause fill-in information provided within Attachment 2. Price: The total price will be evalauted for fair and reasonableness. Cybersecurity Verification: Affirmation that the contractor meets CMMC Level 1 requirements with an active self-assessment entered in SPRS. Vendor Administrative Information: Company Name, Physical Address, Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, Email), SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), CAGE Code, and Verification of Small Business Status under NAICS 238210. A written notice of award, or acceptance of an offer, mailed or otherwise furnished to the successful offeror within the time for acceptance specified in the offer, shall result in a binding contract without further action by either party. Before the offer�s specified expiration time, the Government may accept an offer, or part of an offer, whether or not there are negotiations after its receipt, unless a written notice of withdrawal is received before award. One award will be made under this solicitation. Awards will be conducted under the provisions of RFO Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. Submit only written offers via e-mail; oral offers will not be accepted. All offerors must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM). 7. RESPONSES QUESTIONS REGARDING THIS SOLICITATION ARE DUE BY Wednesday, 21 October 2026 on or before 12:00 PM Pacific Daylight Time (PDT). OFFERS ARE DUE BY Monday, 2 November 2026 at 6:30 AM Pacific Standard Time (PST). All submissions are to be sent via email to Contract Specialist Elsa Ortiz Aguilar at elsa.ortiz_aguilar@us.af.mil and Contracting Officer Suzanna Kussman at suzanna.kussman@us.af.mil, via electronic email. No late submissions will be accepted.
